newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes bolt higher on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes bolt higher on supply concerns.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes leapt higher Monday, treading into lofty price territory on the back of an extended rally for extremely bullish NYMEX futures.

Cash traders in the U.S. Gulf said domestic grade barrels also attracted firmer deals, reflecting stronger prices for key North Sea crudes, and expectations for tighter foreign supplies in the immediate term.

June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing added around $1.00 to its benchmark value by late Monday, talked at $21.35-45 a barrel. Recent bearishness for front month prices evaporated, with June WTI/Cushing holding a 10-14 cents advantage over July from session start to close.
"It seems there are about 11 different things that could pop the market higher, with all the political tensions around," said a cash trader in Texas.
Some of those nearly dozen possibilities streamed into the market Monday. Reports from the notoriously tense Middle East and a surprising fisherman protest in the North Sea keyed the news.

Angry fisherman staged a blockade of Britain's Sullom Voe crude export terminal, which exports an average of 480,000 barrels per day of crude. A small flotilla of vessels were expected to meet with eviction by Tuesday, when a tanker is due to arrive at the port.
The fishermen were protesting delays in compensatory payments resulting from suits filed following the 1993 Braer tanker accident.
Traders said existing bullishness for Brent prices, and expectations for a significant reduction in June output due to planned maintenance, also perked-up U.S. crude differentials.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold late Monday at a 10 cents premium to marker June WTI/Cushing, within today's trading range from 9-12 cents over WTI. Prices reflect a 3-6 cents gain for the key sweet barometer.
"I expect the market to go higher, given the backwardation in Brent spreads, firmer CFD's and tight supplies for the rest of June," said a cash player in the Gulf.

In the Middle East, Iran began six days of fresh wargames in the Strait of Hormuz Sunday, prompting U.S. military commanders to vow vigilence against any attempt to disrupt vital oil flows through the world's strategic waterway for crude exports.
For the rest of the grades, West Texas Sour/Midland sold firmer at $1.42 and $1.44 under the marker, with Eugene Island talked at $1.50-44 under June WTI/Cushing.
Midland/WTI failed to budge from existing price levels around 30 cents under benchmark, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire ranged around 35 cents cheaper.
WTI/Cushing Postings were firmer on the back of expanding June/July rolls at $2.15-$2.19.
